title: Why Do Apples Float but Potatoes Sink? 🍎
description:
Why do apples float in water while potatoes sink? About a quarter of an apple is air trapped between its cells, so it's less dense than water, while a potato is packed with heavy starch grains.

Sources:

topic: Why do apples float but potatoes sink?
script: Your apple is twenty-five percent air. Your potato isn't. That's why one floats and one sinks. Drop both into a bowl of water. The apple bobs right back up. The potato heads straight for the bottom. The secret is density. Anything lighter than the same amount of water floats. Inside an apple, the cells aren't packed tightly. Between them are tiny pockets of air, about a quarter of the whole apple. So the apple ends up lighter than water, like a life jacket made of fruit. A potato is different. Its cells are stuffed with grains of starch, and starch is heavier than water. There's hardly any air in there, so down it goes. That's why bobbing for apples works. If apples sank, the game would be impossible! So what else in your kitchen is secretly full of air?
key_facts: About 25% of an apple's volume is air in pockets between its cells
That makes an apple less dense than water, so it floats
Potato cells are packed with starch grains; starch is denser than water
A potato's specific gravity is roughly 1.06-1.10, so it sinks
